sheets.name: Cafe brunch
sheets.intro: Brunch is almost all green once the yolks are firm. Here is the benny trap and everything around it, on one screen.

rows.text: Eggs benedict is the trap: the poached yolk runs and hollandaise is a raw-egg sauce. Ask for the eggs firm and the hollandaise left off, then add smashed avo or a hot grilled tomato.
Cafe-made mayo and aioli are raw egg. Jar mayo and commercial aioli are pasteurised, so just ask which one lands on the plate.
Smoked salmon is cold-smoked and never actually cooked. Canned salmon with cream cheese on a toasted bagel scratches the same itch.
Cold ham, prosciutto or salami on the board carries listeria. Ask for it crisped hot in the pan and it is back on.
Brie, feta, ricotta and goat cheese on the toast only count once they are cooked and bubbling hot. Cold and crumbled is a no, baked is a yes.
The cold-press juice and the smoothie bar use pre-cut fruit and machines that are hard to clean. A bottled pasteurised juice or a blender at home is the fix.
Coffee is absolutely on: keep the whole day under 200mg of caffeine, which is about 1 to 2 espresso coffees. Decaf takes over after that.
The big brekky is all clear: firm-yolk eggs, hot bacon, grilled mushrooms, hash browns, smashed avo and toast.

asks: Can I get the eggs cooked firm, please?
Is the mayo or aioli from a jar?
Can that come without the hollandaise?

sheets.name: Pub
sheets.intro: Parmy yes, steak well done, wine list on pause. The pub menu is friendlier than it looks.

rows.text: Rare and medium-rare steak is a toxoplasmosis risk. Ordered well done with no pink left, steak is back on the table.
There is no safe amount of alcohol, so the wine and the espresso martini both sit this one out. Soda, lime and frozen berries in a proper glass still feels like a night out.
Pâté, parfait and terrine on the starters are chilled meat spreads: listeria plus a lot of vitamin A. A shelf-stable jar pâté at home is the safe version.
Caesar salad dressing is traditionally raw egg, and the cured meat on top is cold. Ask for a bottled dressing and hot grilled chicken.
Oysters natural and the cold prawn plate are ready-to-eat seafood. Kilpatrick and hot garlic prawns are the same craving, cooked.
Flake in the beer batter is shark: one 150g serve a fortnight, and no other fish in that fortnight. Ask what the fish of the day actually is.
The parmy is a legend and completely fine: chicken cooked through, ham grilled hot under bubbling cheese.
Well-done burgers, schnitzels, hot pies, chips and a roast dinner are all green when they arrive hot.

asks: Can I get the steak well done, please?
Is the fish of the day flake?
Is the salad dressing made here or out of a bottle?

sheets.name: Sushi train
sheets.intro: Fresh plus cooked wins every time. It is raw fish and sitting time that get benched, not sushi itself.

rows.text: Sashimi, nigiri and anything raw is off for now. Ask the kitchen for a fresh roll with cooked chicken, cooked egg or veg instead.
Smoked salmon rolls count as raw too, because cold-smoked fish is never cooked. A teriyaki chicken roll is the swap.
Plates that have been circling a while are out even with cooked fillings, because sitting time is the listeria risk. Order off the menu so it is made fresh.
Pre-packed sushi from a supermarket or servo fridge is the same problem: made hours ago and kept cold. Made in front of you is the green version.
Cold cooked prawn on top of a plate counts as pre-cooked cold seafood. Hot prawn tempura, straight from the fryer, is all clear.
Made to order with cooked fillings and eaten straight away is the green lane: teriyaki chicken, cooked egg, avo, cucumber, tinned tuna with jar mayo.
Anything hot from the kitchen is easy: karaage chicken, gyoza, katsu curry, miso soup and edamame.

asks: Can you make that one fresh for me with cooked fillings?
Is there any raw or smoked fish in this roll?
How long has that plate been on the belt?

sheets.name: Pizza
sheets.intro: The easiest menu in the game. A screaming hot oven fixes nearly everything, including the ham and the salami.

rows.text: Prosciutto draped on after the oven stays cold and cured. Ask for it baked on so it crisps up, and it is a green light.
Fresh mozzarella, bocconcini or burrata scattered on at the end never gets hot. Melted through under the heat, it is fine.
A cold feta or ricotta crumble added after baking misses the oven. Ask for the soft cheese cooked on instead.
House-made aioli or garlic dip on the side can be raw egg. Stick to a commercial bottle, or go with the tomato sugo.
Ham, salami, pepperoni and bacon baked onto the pizza are all clear. The oven does the work that heating deli meat at home would do.
Melted mozzarella, mushrooms, olives, capsicum and pineapple are green. Pineapple will not start labour either, promise.
Leftover slices are fine the next day: back through a hot oven until they are steaming, not straight from the fridge.

asks: Can you cook the prosciutto on the pizza rather than adding it after?
Is the mozzarella baked on, or added fresh at the end?
Is the garlic dip out of a bottle?

sheets.name: Fish and chips
sheets.intro: Straight out of the fryer is a green light. The only real question at the counter is what the fish actually is.

rows.text: Prawn cocktail and the chilled prawns in the cabinet are pre-cooked cold seafood. Ask for them hot in a garlic prawn dish instead.
Raw oysters off the ice are out, but oysters Kilpatrick straight off the grill are very much in.
Flake IS shark. One 150g serve a fortnight, and no other fish in that fortnight. Snapper, whiting or flathead comes with no cap.
Swordfish, broadbill and marlin sit under the same fortnight rule as flake.
Orange roughy, sold as sea perch, and catfish are once a week with no other fish that week.
Battered or grilled snapper, whiting, flathead and barra, hot from the fryer, are the good news: 1 to 3 serves of fish a week is encouraged.
Hot chips, potato cakes, calamari and dim sims are all green when they land hot. Chicken salt included.
Tartare sauce from a commercial bottle or a squeeze pack is pasteurised and fine.

asks: Is the fish of the day flake?
What fish is in the battered fillet today?
Is the tartare sauce out of a bottle?

sheets.name: Maccas
sheets.intro: Drive-through, sorted. The burgers are fine, it is the ice cream machine that gets benched.

rows.text: Soft serve cones, sundaes, McFlurry and thickshakes all come out of the dispenser machine, which is hard to clean right through. A choc top or a scoop from a tub is the fix.
Pre-packaged sandwiches, wraps and salads from a fridge cabinet, the servo next door included, are made ahead and kept cold. Anything hot off the grill beats them.
Fancier burger joints often use a house-made aioli, which is raw egg. The big chains use commercial sauces, so ask if you are anywhere boutique.
The McCafe latte draws on the same 200mg daily caffeine budget as any other coffee.
Burgers, cheeseburgers and quarter pounders are all clear. Fast-food patties get cooked hard and fast, so there is no pink left.
Nuggets, fries and a hot apple pie are green, straight from the fryer to the bag.
Still craving the cone? A tub ice cream sundae at home, or a frozen banana blitzed with a splash of milk, does the job.

asks: Is that sauce a commercial one from a bottle?
Can I get this one hot and fresh, please?

sheets.name: Thai and Chinese
sheets.intro: Hot, fresh and straight from the wok is exactly what we want. Sprouts are the one regular thing to ask about.

rows.text: Raw bean sprouts piled on the pad thai or the pho are a listeria carrier. Ask for them cooked right through or left out, and the dish is green.
Rare beef in pho only gets flashed by the broth. Ask for the beef well done, or order the chicken one.
Enoki mushrooms in a hotpot often go in at the last second. Give them a proper simmer until they are cooked through and they are fine.
Fried ice cream has an egg batter that often does not cook through. A scoop from a tub with a hot sauce over it is the safe version.
Chinese tea and Thai iced tea count toward the 200mg daily caffeine budget.
Stir-fries, curries, steamed rice, dumplings, san choy bow and soups are the green lane whenever they arrive steaming hot.
Fried rice is fine made fresh with the egg cooked firm. Leftovers get cooled fast, reheated once, and eaten within a day.

asks: Can I get the sprouts cooked right through, or left out?
Is the beef in the pho cooked well done?
Can that come out fresh from the wok rather than the bain-marie?
